summary.short: Pennsylvania House Bill 1063 (2023, introduced) would create a misdemeanor offense of unlawfully disseminating an artificially generated depiction of an individual with intent to harass, annoy or alarm, and extend child sexual abuse and minor image offenses to such depictions. Takes effect in 60 days.
summary.long: As introduced on 28 April 2023 and referred to the House Judiciary Committee, the bill amends Title 18 (Crimes and Offenses) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes. Section 1 adds 18 Pa.C.S. § 3131.1, which makes it an offense to disseminate an artificially generated depiction of an individual with intent to harass, annoy or alarm that individual. An artificially generated depiction is a visual depiction that appears to authentically show an individual in nudity or sexual conduct that did not occur, produced substantially through technical means such as artificial intelligence or photoshop software. Consent of the depicted individual is a defense. Grading is a first-degree misdemeanor when the depicted individual is a minor and a second-degree misdemeanor otherwise. A person may be convicted if the victim or offender is located in Pennsylvania. The Attorney General receives concurrent authority to investigate and prosecute violations involving more than one county or another state. Law enforcement officers acting in official duties are excluded. Sections 2 and 3 extend the child sexual abuse offense (§ 6312) and the offense of transmission of sexually explicit images by a minor (§ 6321) to artificially generated depictions of minors and add related definitions. Section 4 provides that the act takes effect in 60 days.

notes: Introduced text (PN 1077, HB 1063, 28 Apr 2023; referred to Judiciary). Definitions of 'artificially generated depiction' differ across the three sections: § 3131.1(g) covers an individual appearing in nudity or sexual conduct; § 6312(g) covers a child under 18 in a prohibited sexual act; § 6321(g) covers a child under 18 in conduct, an action or nudity. Sections 2 and 3 state amendments to existing definitions and to § 6312(c), (d), (f)(3) but reproduce only the new wording without marking prior text. Terms such as 'Minor', 'Nudity', 'Sexual conduct' and 'Visual depiction' are defined by reference to §§ 3131, 5903(e) and 6321 and those provisions are not reproduced. Intra-Title 18 cross-references (e.g., §§ 5903, 6312, 6321 in § 3131.1(a)) are not separate relation rows. target_instrument_id is left empty where the target is not in the registry.
